messages.author: 9eada87ac9c1c9b2
messages.subject: parboot "non-finite finite-difference value" error
parts:
Hello all,

I am currently fitting generalized distance sampling models in unmarked on some avian point-count data using the gdistsamp function, but I am having trouble getting a parametric bootstrap to reach completion on my AIC-best model. I repeatedly receive a "non-finite finite-difference value" error somewhere between 0-20% of the process. Strangely enough, the bootstrap performs fine when I use a half-normal detection function instead of a hazard, but the hazard is far preferred by AIC. I read that changing the optimization method to "Nelder-Mead" may improve bootstrap performance, but then I run into issues with convergence, even at very low numbers of K. I should mention that it is a small dataset with 88 points, two visits, and four distance bins. I standardized all continuous covariates before modeling. Any recommendations?

My top model (seven parameters):
summary(fm12 <- gdistsamp(lambdaformula=~YEAR, phiformula=~Visit-1, pformula=~Observ, SCTA.umf, keyfun = "hazard", output = c("density"), unitsOut = "ha", mixture = "P", se = TRUE, engine= "C", threads=8))

note: YEAR is a continuous covariate of year of last forest management

Bootstrap code:
pb12 <- parboot(fm12, fitstats, nsim=100, report=5)

Error:
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :
2 nodes produced errors; first error: non-finite finite-difference value [4]

Thanks in advance for the help!

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] parboot "non-finite finite-difference value" error
parts:
How do the actual estimates from the top model look? If some parameter estimates or SEs are very large, that can result in parboot simulated datasets that the model can't successfully fit. In that case you'd want to determine if the top model is actually usable or perhaps needs to be simplified.

If you're confident the top model estimates are reasonable, you can try installing the dev version of unmarked from Github. We recently made some changes to parboot to better handle errors like you're seeing, but they haven't made it to the CRAN version yet.

Ken

Tyler,

I agree with Marc, I think the estimates look OK. In general I have found unmarked struggles with the hazard-rate more than the other key functions which might be the reason for parboot's issues. The dev version should solve this, it just skips over any simulations that error instead of stopping entirely.

Ken

> > > then I run into issues with convergence, even at very low numbers of K.

> > and
> > > four distance bins. I standardized all continuous covariates before
> > > modeling. Any recommendations?

Ken
